comment: Ursa's own register table. The algorithm lives in the vendored merge-register.py; the paths and flags live here, in this repository, because a borrowed tool that carries its own file list answers about files this repository does not have (Ursa INC-2026-10-18-hq-tool-paths-are-hq-s). tools/registers/merge-driver.mjs reads this file, matches git's %P against `path`, and refuses by name when the path is not declared.

registers.why: Two seats append to its tail: the PM's pass and the exo seat's window. They collided on 2026-10-24 between PR #301 and PR #302 and cost a hand resolution. Entries 1 through 18 are numbers and everything from 2026-10-18 is an INC- slug, so the identifier pattern has to admit both forms; the register's own header freezes the old numbers and forbids allocating 19.
registers.why_identifier: Measured, not assumed. With --heading alone, two branches that both append `## Incident 19 — <different title>` merge to exit 0 and publish two entries answering to one citable name. With --identifier the same merge is refused by name. The slug case behaves identically: two seats filing `INC-2026-10-24-dup-slug` with different titles are refused instead of both landing.

registers.why: The PM, the chair and the exo seat all append ADRs and Findings here, and both PRs in the 2026-10-24 collision touched it as well. Numbered rather than dated, and the number is allocated by reading the tail, which is the case the --identifier exception exists for.
registers.why_identifier: This register already holds ADR-005 and ADR-006 twice each on `main` (exo found it on 2026-10-18 and it is still open). The merger tolerates a duplicate that predates the merge, by design, and refuses one the merge itself would mint, so enabling this guards the file from getting worse without demanding that the existing repair happen first. Verified on the real file: two appends of ADR-007 and ADR-008 over today's `main` exit 0 and keep 13 entries.

registers.why: Two seats' work lands in it and it is the largest register this seat keeps (6,760 lines), so it is the file a split or a concurrent append collides on most expensively. Enabled 2026-10-25 by the forty-second window after measuring that the blocker this entry recorded is gone: the file held '## Compounding ratio' twice when this table was written, and today all 40 of its '## ' headings are unique, so the merger no longer refuses at parse. The condition this entry set for flipping it was 'once the heading is unique', and that is the condition that was checked rather than the claim being taken forward.
registers.why_identifier: Deliberately null. The entries are dated window headings with a free-text trigger in parentheses, so there is no short stable name to key on, and heading identity is the whole key. Verified on a synthetic two-sided append over the real 6,760-line file: two different new window entries at the tail merge at exit 0 keeping both, where plain git reports CONFLICT (content).

registers.why: Already covered by the older driver, tools/ledger/union-merge.mjs, which is kept rather than replaced today. Its grammar carries a second block kind this merger has no flag for: the chair's top-level dated note bullets (`- 2026-10-05 (chair): ...`), which are entries in the ledger and would be swallowed into whichever entry precedes them here. Moving the ledger across is a separate change with its own risk, and it is ledger entry 2 of this run rather than a line in this table.

Deliberately excluded even though HQ's own lessons file names it as needing this. It is vendored from HQ and no Ursa seat appends to it, so every change to it arrives as a whole-file sync. An entry-keyed merge of a vendored sync would resolve by keeping both sides' entries, which is exactly how a stale local copy survives a sync that was supposed to replace it.
